sources.title: Excavations at Sarutaru: A Neolithic Site in Assam
sources.publication: Man and Environment 1; pagination variously cited 39–42 or 39–43, verify scan before final bibliography

sources.access_status: Indexed opening text consulted; PDF recognized as 94-page container, but no page images successfully fetched
sources.consulted_locator: Opening report paragraphs and The site section in indexed excerpt; printed page not verified
claims: Rao reports excavation during 1967–73 under Dibrugarh University's Anthropology department.
The report places Sarutaru approximately 25 km southeast of Guwahati, on a small hillock at the Shillong plateau/Brahmaputra plain margin, with the Digaru river on the northern side.
Rao distinguishes stratified Daojali Hading finds from earlier surface or household collections of celts.
sources.geographic_scope: Present-day Assam evidence; Shillong plateau setting does not mean the site is necessarily in present Meghalaya.
conflicts: Later reconnaissance papers sometimes say 1971–74; use original report dates provisionally and verify season records.
Indexed rainfall figures in this old report appear implausible if understood as annual mm; do not reuse them without original units and modern meteorological checking.
sources.research_gap: Read pages 39–43 and all plates; verify trench details, artefact counts, pottery manufacture and figure/plate captions directly.

sources.title: Luminescence Dating of Neolithic Pottery in North East India
sources.access_status: Author publication abstract consulted and IITG bibliography confirmed; full paper inaccessible through tested URL
sources.consulted_locator: Abstract; paper spans printed pages 492–496, individual figure locators not verified
claims: Authors report OSL dating of excavated pottery: Daojali Hading sample LD1728 gives 2.7 ± 0.3 ka; Gawak Abri LD1727 gives 2.3 ± 0.2 ka.
These are pottery luminescence estimates, not radiocarbon dates or proof of the earliest arrival of humans.
Daojali Hading is in Dima Hasao, Assam; Gawak Abri is a Meghalaya comparison.
conflicts: An indexed IITG thesis Table 1.3 puts 2.7 ± 0.3 ka under a 14C heading. Do not inherit that mislabel.
Do not silently convert ka to an exact BCE date until the study's reference year and reporting conventions are checked.
sources.research_gap: Obtain full primary paper; inspect dose rates, sample provenance, uncertainty, reference-year conventions, number of samples and photos.

sources.access_status: Publisher abstract, metadata and reference list consulted; full article access restricted

claims: Study analyzes seven charcoal samples, five potsherds and five sediment samples from test pits.
Publisher abstract reports approximately 240–1379 CE for the analyzed material, despite Neolithic classification of a nearby reported site.
Ground/polished axes, pottery and megaliths occur in the archaeological record of the valley.
sources.geographic_scope: Assam-Meghalaya foothill study; individual dated sites cannot be assigned to Assam without full sample table and site coordinates.
conflicts: Tool form and cord marking alone cannot securely establish a prehistoric calendar age. The date range cannot be transferred to Sarutaru, Marakdola or Daojali without sample-level proof.
sources.research_gap: Acquire sample table, calibration results, laboratory IDs, stratigraphy, site coordinates and supplementary data before using calendar ranges in a chapter.
